title: PE/COFF header (Windows executable)
summary: A Windows PE (Portable Executable) file begins with a DOS stub (MZ header + 'This program cannot be run in DOS mode'), then at the PE header offset (e_lfanew) a 4-byte signature 'PE\x00\x00' followed by a 20-byte COFF file header and an optional header (PE32 or PE32+).

ext.summary: A Windows PE (Portable Executable) file begins with a DOS stub (MZ header + 'This program cannot be run in DOS mode'), then at the PE header offset (e_lfanew) a 4-byte signature 'PE\x00\x00' followed by a 20-byte COFF file header and an optional header (PE32 or PE32+).

structure.meaning: File offset (at DOS header offset 0x3C) to the PE signature.
Target CPU: 0x014C i386, 0x8664 x86-64, 0x01C0 ARM, 0xAA64 ARM64.
Count of section headers following the optional header.
Offset to COFF symbol table (0 if stripped).
Number of symbols in the symbol table.
Size of the optional header (224 for PE32, 240 for PE32+).
Flags: executable image, DLL, large address aware, ... (e.g. 0x0002 EXECUTABLE_IMAGE, 0x2000 DLL).
RVA of the entry point (relative to image base).
Preferred load address (PE32 4 bytes, PE32+ 8 bytes).
Alignment of sections in the file (usually 0x200).

notes: 'MZ' = Mark Zbikowski, the DOS header designer.
e_lfanew at offset 0x3C points to the PE signature; typically 0x80 or 0xE8.
Section headers follow the optional header: Name (8 bytes), VirtualSize, VirtualAddress, SizeOfRawData, PointerToRawData, ..., Characteristics.
PE32+ (0x20B) drops BaseOfData and widens ImageBase/SizeOfStackReserve/SizeOfStackCommit/SizeOfHeapReserve/SizeOfHeapCommit to 8 bytes.
